You are in an **Archon Horizon** workspace at `.`.

Load the **`horizon`** skill FIRST. Read it at the ABSOLUTE path
`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` (also exported as `$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`) — do NOT use a
relative path like `.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`, which fails when your
shell starts in a member project rather than the workspace root. The skill
explains where the state lives, the tools, and this workspace's conventions
(one-shot discipline, git commits, the final report).

Before modifying files, inspect the required and conversational inbox lanes:
`"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json`
then `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json`.
Protections are standing constraints even when already read. Address or explicitly
acknowledge unread conversations before ordinary advisory inbox material.

# Task
Task: ajcr-p4
Title: AJCR prover p4: claim and close the 4th-most important representability item
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
References: roadmap=AJCR.jacobian,AJCR.w4-rep,AJCR.w4-rep.datum; inbox=I-0838

You are prover lane `ajcr-p4` on Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild. This round the objective is deliberately FREE: nobody has told you which declaration to prove. Your objective is to identify the FOURTH most important open item standing between this project and Picard/Pic^0 representability, claim it publicly, and discharge it.

READ FIRST: protection item `I-0838`. It is the claim protocol for this round's ten parallel lanes and it is not optional — steps 2 through 5 (check ownership, claim with `roadmap set --owner ajcr-p4`, announce, release on exit) are what stop four lanes proving the same lemma. Also read `I-0491` and `I-0492`, the two binding human decisions, before touching the seam.

YOUR RANK. You take the FOURTH most important item. Rank is a tie-break so four lanes do not converge on one target, not a fence: if your item turns out to be blocked on another lane's, say so in the inbox and swap. On a contested item you yield to p1, p2 or p3, then take the next.

YOUR PEERS this round are ajcr-p1, ajcr-p2, ajcr-p3, ajcr-p4 plus the reviewer `review-ajcr`. The reviewer is auditing route and organisation and will be correcting the board in its first hour — read its inbox items before you fix your target, and re-read them if you are about to start something large. It may direct-message you a proposal; weigh it against what you hold, and take it if it is genuinely worth more. You may propose work to the other lanes the same way (`inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane>`), naming declaration, file, and why it beats what they hold.

HOW TO CHOOSE, since this is the part I am delegating to you. "Most important" means: measured against the project's representability headline, what does discharging this buy? A leaf that unblocks three others beats a leaf that is merely nearest. A leaf whose stated prerequisite turns out to already exist in the file beats both — earlier sessions' costings in this workspace have been wrong in that direction more than once, so read the actual Lean hypothesis, not the prose about it. Use `horizon graph -p Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild frontier` for the ranked view, `horizon roadmap list --focus AJCR.w4-rep` for the board, and `horizon search` (which spans both projects AND mathlib) before you prove anything — the premise you need is often already next door under a name you would not have grepped.

THE BAR, and it is higher than usual this round. An audit on 2026-07-29 sampled 101 representability claims across both projects and refuted 99: 67 were sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 proved something adjacent to what they claimed, 3 did not exist. So:
- Sorry-free is necessary, not sufficient. Before you report a gate closed, exhibit a witness for EVERY antecedent, or state plainly which antecedent remains undischarged. "The implication is proved" and "the conclusion holds for some curve" are different claims and I want to know which you have.
- Never introduce a class, structure field, or side condition whose statement does not mention the object it is about. The cautionary case is `HasDivFunctor`: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, the curve did not occur, and the blueprint advertised it as the existence of the divisor functor with `\leanok`. It survived because nobody read the statement.
- Never discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed. `choose_spec.1` of your own binder is `P → P`.
- A green build is not evidence of non-vacuity, and `lean_multi_attempt` reports every snippet as closing the goal when the file's imports are stale. Check imports before believing a probe.
- Do not restate an obligation more weakly to make a count go down. If you cannot close it, leave it open and say why.

ONE SHARED LEDGER, ten writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once — write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`. Commit at every coherent point; an interrupted lane loses only what was uncommitted. Follow the `lean-check` LSP loop for edits and keep `lake build` for the session boundary — nine other lanes want the build lock too.

WHERE THIS PROJECT ACTUALLY STANDS, so you do not rediscover it. AJCR is the architecturally sound one. `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) and `mixedParamRepresentableBy` (`Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125`) are genuinely sorry-free and kernel-confirmed on `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` — honest, non-circular implications that WOULD produce a real representing scheme. The problem is that all three antecedents are undischarged, with no sorry-free witness for any: `IsChartUniv`, Zariski-local surjectivity of `Sigma.desc f`, and `rep i`. A correct machine with nothing to feed it.

That makes your choice unusually concrete: pick whichever of the three missing inputs you judge closest, or the leaf that most directly produces one. Do not treat the sorry count as the map — the 17 body sorries are 15 in `Challenge.lean` (the statement-only headline file, so those ARE the north star, not debt) and 2 in `Pic0ThetaCocycle.lean`. The real work is antecedents that no sorry marks.

The board under `AJCR.w4-rep` (51/74 done) has a deep tail worth reading with suspicion: under `datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate`, four siblings are `rejected` (`cert-relocalize`, `joint-cover`, `leak-image`, `tube-fibre`) and one is `blocked` (`away-kerspan`). Four rejections clustered under one parent usually means the parent's formulation is wrong, not that four different approaches each independently failed. The reviewer is determining which; read its finding before you spend a session inside that tail. Other open items to weigh: `datum.dat-b` (coverage + injectivity — every pic^0 point is hit), `datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus` and its `chart-u` child (the co-signed chartLocus and its openness — the sole gate of dat-b B-6 AND the whole dat-glue), `datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep.u2` (the DDR9-U epsilon-identity at the universal point), `datum.dat-glue` (the 01JJ RepresentableBy assembly), `datum.dat-j`, `datum.dat-g`, `w4-rep.build-reach` (93 of 620 modules unrooted, so the axiom probe does not see them — a file nobody imports is a file nobody has measured, which may matter to whichever "sorry-free" claim you are relying on).

Costings in this project have been wrong before, in the expensive direction: a handoff demanded a new structure field where the localization lemma it asked for was already in the file. So for whatever leaf you pick, read its actual Lean hypothesis before accepting its stated price. An over-priced leaf is where you win this round.

The sibling project Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge is readable and `horizon search` spans both. It has more Quot/Serre machinery than this project does; if your leaf needs cohomological input, look there before building it. Price the consumer's carrier when you do — a cross-project match at object level can be true and irrelevant if the cover or instance your statement binds differs.

WHAT I WANT AT THE END. Your report should answer three things without me having to ask: which item you claimed and why it was the fourth-most important, what its state is now (closed sorry-free with all antecedents witnessed / closed as an implication with named antecedents still open / advanced with the remaining obligation stated / blocked, with the blocker), and what you learned that changes another lane's plan. If you found a costing wrong, a vacuity, or a route problem, that goes in the inbox as an `issue` at the site that made the claim — not only in your report, which nobody downstream reads.

If your first-choice item collapses on inspection — the prerequisite already exists, or the statement turns out vacuous, or another lane got there first — that is a finding, not a wasted session. Record it, release the claim, and take the next item. Do not sit on a claimed item you are not working.

This is a headless, one-shot session: advance the REAL objective, commit each
verified unit and any final edits, keep operational comments to the delta,
then write the skill's brief final report.

1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289

296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and

303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309

311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,

313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.

316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.

321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtCoverBridge
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.OverSigmaExtension
8	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Representability
9	
10	/-!
11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
12	
13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/
41	
42	set_option autoImplicit false
43	
44	universe u
45	
46	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
47	
48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
49	
50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
51	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
52	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
53	
54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl
70	
71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem
143	
144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩
150	
151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
152	
153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice
170	
171	end AlgebraicGeometry

# Producing the Jacobian representability datum from a Zariski chart family

The pinned datum `JacobianData C` of the curve `C` bundles a representing object for the
degree-zero Picard functor together with the two finiteness certificates of that object.
This file constructs it: first from a bare representation (`JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy`),

    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (yoneda.map g) :=
  MorphismProperty.relative_map (P := @IsOpenImmersion) (F := yoneda) ‹IsOpenImmersion g›

/-! ## The restricted chart map -/

/-- **The chart map restricted to an open of its source.**

`f` is the unrestricted chart map (in practice `abelSigmaChart`, whose source is the divisor
scheme) and `V` an open subscheme of the source; the restriction is the composition with the
yoneda image of the open inclusion.

The point of restricting is that the unrestricted Abel map is *not* an open immersion of
presheaves — see the `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep` header — while its restriction to the locus where
the fibre is a single point is.  This definition is neutral about which open `V` is; the
chart-locus choice enters only in the certificate. -/
def restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (V : X.Opens) : yoneda.obj (V : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
  yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f

/-- **The composition half of the `hf` certificate**: a restriction of an open immersion of
presheaves along an open immersion is again one.

`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is `MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda`, which is stable under
composition (`MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`, needing `yoneda` full and
faithful and `IsOpenImmersion` stable under composition — all instances).  Together with

part of C9b that is bookkeeping.

uniqueness of the normalized effective representative (DAT-C GAP-2) and the classifier.  A
lane must not read this lemma as reducing C9b to plumbing; it isolates the plumbing so the
mathematics is visible. -/
theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}}
    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (V : X.Opens)
    (hfV : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :
    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart f V) :=
  MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition.comp_mem _ _
    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map V.ι) hfV

statement.  It is pinned here as a definition so that the gate has a name in Lean and not
only in a worksheet — the pattern `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.IsChartDatumPresentation` uses.

/-- **CHART-U(c), pinned**: the chart map is an open immersion of presheaves after restriction
to the locus where the fibre class has a unique effective representative.

This is the whole remaining content of C9b's `hf`.  Stated as a `Prop`-valued definition
rather than proved, because its proof needs the *relative* form of GAP-2 over `chartLocus`
together with `divRepClassifyZar`; a lane that discharges it gets `hf` by feeding it to

(`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`), and keeping the two apart means neither has to wait for the
other. -/
def IsChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
    (V : D.left.Opens) : Prop :=
  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V)

/-- The pinned obligation is exactly what `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` would
give from an unrestricted certificate — recorded so that no lane proves the same thing
twice, and so that the *reason* the unrestricted route is unavailable stays visible: the
hypothesis of that lemma is false for the Abel chart at `V = ⊤`. -/
lemma isChartUniv_of_unrestricted {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
    (V : D.left.Opens)
    (h : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg)) :
    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V h

/-! ## The structure morphism of a restricted chart -/

/-- **The structure morphism of a restricted chart is the restriction of the structure
morphism.**  Hence the `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom …)` hypothesis of
`JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited by every restriction: being locally of finite type is
local on the source, and an open immersion is locally of finite type.

Concretely, for the Abel chart of a representation `rep` by `D` the unrestricted structure
morphism is `D.hom` (`chartHom_abelSigmaChart`, `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:212`), so a
restricted Abel chart over `V ⊆ D.left` has structure morphism `V.ι ≫ D.hom`. -/
lemma chartHom_restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (V : X.Opens) {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => restrictChart f V) i
      = V.ι ≫ chartHom C (fun _ : ι => f) i := by
  change (yonedaEquiv (yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f)).1 = V.ι ≫ (yonedaEquiv f).1
  -- Both sides are the Σ-component of the universal element restricted along `V.ι`:
  -- the `Over.sigmaExtension` transition map precomposes the structure morphism, and
  -- `f`'s naturality moves the restriction across `f`.
  rw [yonedaEquiv_comp, yonedaEquiv_yoneda_map]
  have hnat := congrArg Sigma.fst
    (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (f.naturality (V.ι).op) (𝟙 X))
  refine hnat.trans ?_
  exact Over.sigmaExtension_map_fst (V.ι) _

end

# DAT-B B-5: the coverage obligation is Zariski-local in the test, so AFFINE tests suffice

`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduced `ChartsCoverLocally` — and with it
antecedent 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` — to pointwise data at **every test scheme
`T`**.  That is where the reduction chain stops, and the quantifier it stops at is the
problem this file addresses.

**Every divisor-side producer in this project is indexed by a RING, not by a scheme.**
`DivFamZar C S π n` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:235`) is a quotient of local-equation
systems over an algebra `S`; `divFamZar C π n T` at a general test
(`Picard/DivisorFamilyZarVehicle.lean:187`) is the affine-opens *limit* of those, and the
comparison `divFamZarAffineEquiv` (:300) collapses it to `DivFamZar` only on an affine
test.  Likewise every producer of a certified family, of an effective witness
(`DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:147`), and every classifier
(`effectiveDivisorClassifyZar`, :217) is stated over a ring or a field.  So a coverage
lane facing "for every scheme `T`" has to cross the affine-to-general gap **before** it can
use any of that machinery, and nothing said it was allowed to skip it.

It is allowed to skip it, and that is this file's content.

## Why locality in the test is not bookkeeping the producer can inline

The naive argument — "sieves are local, so restrict to an affine cover" — is not available
as stated, because `ChartsCoverLocally` is a statement about the sieve on `T` itself, and
the pointwise hypothesis quantifies over points of `T`.  Three things have to be checked,
and each is where the argument could fail:

* **the class must restrict.**  The datum at a point `t` of an affine piece `Y` is about a
  section over an open of `Y`, while the obligation at `t : ↥T` is about an open of `T`.
  Composing `W.ι ≫ 𝒰.f j` gives a map into `T` but not an *open of* `T`, so the transport
  cannot be done at the level of `T.Opens` — it has to be done at the level of the sieve,
  where an arbitrary morphism is allowed;
* **the sieve must be transitive.**  Membership of `⨆ i, imageSieve (f i) s` in the
  topology on `T` is deduced from membership of its *pullbacks* along the cover maps, which
  is `GrothendieckTopology.transitive` plus `Presheaf.pullback_imageSieve` — the latter is
  what says the pullback of an image sieve is the image sieve of the restricted section,
  i.e. that the obligation at `Y` is about `s|_Y` and nothing else;
* **the pullback must commute with the supremum.**  `Sieve.pullback` is a left adjoint on
  sieves, so it preserves `iSup`; without that the per-piece obligations would be about a
  different sieve than the one the pullback of the target names.

None of the three mentions `pic⁰`, a chart, or a divisor.  That is the point: the
affine-to-general passage for antecedent 2 is a fact about the site, and mixing it with the
geometry is what made it look like part of the geometry's price.

## What this does and does not buy

It buys the quantifier, and only the quantifier.  `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` below
asks for the pointwise datum **only over affine schemes**, and produces
`ChartsCoverLocally` at every test; `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine` composes that
with B-6.  So a producer may now assume its test is `Spec S` and reach for
`divFamZarAffineEquiv`, `DivisorFamilyFieldSurj`, `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` and the rest
of the ring-indexed machinery directly.

It does **not** produce the datum at an affine test.  That is B-5's geometry and it remains
open; per `Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` and the `dat-b` row the residue there is
the class-side question, and per `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean` the range containment `hV` is
a further separate obligation.  What changes is that the residue is now stated where the
tree's producers live.

**On the converse, corrected.**  An earlier version of this paragraph said
`affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally` makes the affine and general forms "equivalent", and cited

affine data by `fun Y _ s y => h Y s y`.  So the affine form is a genuine **weakening** of the
general one, which is exactly why `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` is worth having; the
honest certificate is that theorem, not a no-op converse (audit `I-1023`).  The converse is

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content

Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
statement is what made it look gated. -/

/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**

If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
Zariski covering sieve of `T`.

The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.

Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)

/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/

variable (C) in
/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.

The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
it, and every point `t` of `T`:

* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.

Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.

**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
  intro T s
  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩

variable (C) in
/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.

The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)

/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening

A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/

variable (C) in
/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**

The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.

**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-!
# C9b: `IsChartUniv` reduced to one clause about the chart locus

`Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` splits `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` into the two
clauses mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative` actually conjoins, and gives a criterion whose
input is elementwise.  This file instantiates that criterion at the Abel chart and at
`V := chartLocus`, which is the pair `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.

The point is to make the residue **one named clause about the chart locus** instead of the
whole certificate.  Concretely, the criterion's `ChartFibrePresented` datum has four fields,
and at the Abel chart three of them are supplied here:

| field | at the Abel chart | status |
|---|---|---|
| `W` | `chartLocus` of the test point's class, as an open | **shape supplied here**, but at the
  cost of `haff` — see the retraction below |
| `r` | the divisor family over the locus | the classifier `divRepClassifyZar` |
| `sq` | its class is the test's class | the classifier's own characterisation |
| `exists_factor` | uniqueness of the normalized representative | **the relative form of GAP-2** |

So `W` needs only B-4 (**not** "nothing" — retracted below), `sq` is a property of whatever
`r` is, and the genuine content is
concentrated in `r` (a construction, from the classifier) and `exists_factor` (relative
GAP-2).  This file makes that split machine-checkable: `IsChartLocusFibre` below names
exactly the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple **at the chart locus**, and
`isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` proves `IsChartUniv` from it.

## Why this is not a restatement

A reduction that merely renames its obligation is worthless, and this one is checked against
that failure mode in two directions:

* `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised, so the `W` field is a *shape* a lane
  no longer has to invent.

  **RETRACTED 2026-07-29, second clause only** (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  This
  read "the `W` field costs zero, which is a real reduction of the datum from four fields to
  three".  The cost is not zero: `chartLocusOpens` takes the argument `haff`, and **nothing in
  the tree discharges it**.  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` removed the
  `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis but passes `haff` straight through, as does
  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it; the affine case that would feed it
  (`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`) is itself conditional on
  `IsChartDatumPresentation`, which is dat-b row B-4's named residue and is only half landed.
  So the datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  The
  residue is now named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4's own obligation by
  `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`;
* `isChartLocusFibre_of_isChartUniv` is the **converse**: `IsChartUniv` at the chart locus
  gives injectivity on every test, so a lane cannot obtain `IsChartUniv` while avoiding the
  content of `exists_factor`.  The reduction is therefore an equivalence in the direction
  that matters, not a weakening.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens` — `chartLocus` as an honest `T.Opens`, using the
  unconditional general-test openness.  This is the `V` that `restrictChart` wants.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartLocusFibre` — the residue: the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple

* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` — **the reduction**: that triple
  gives `IsChartUniv` (hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)` pair) at any open.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isChartUniv` — the converse-direction check.
-/
